questions.question: The angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection. This is known as the
questions.explanation: The second law of reflection states that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection, and the incident ray, reflected ray, and normal all lie in the same plane.

questions.question: The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in the
questions.explanation: The first law of reflection states that the incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.

questions.question: The angle of reflection is measured between the reflected ray and the
questions.explanation: By convention, the angle of reflection is measured between the reflected ray and the normal at the point of incidence.

questions.question: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of 30°. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.explanation: According to the second law of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence. Therefore, the angle of reflection is 30°.

questions.question: A ray of light is incident normally on a plane mirror. The angle of reflection is
questions.explanation: When a ray is incident normally, it strikes the mirror along the normal. The angle of incidence is 0°, so the angle of reflection is also 0°.

questions.question: The image formed by a plane mirror is always
questions.explanation: A plane mirror always forms a virtual, erect image of the same size as the object. The image is laterally inverted.

questions.question: The image formed by a plane mirror is as far behind the mirror as the object is
questions.explanation: For a plane mirror, the image distance behind the mirror equals the object distance in front of the mirror. So the image is as far in front of the mirror as the object is in front.

questions.question: The magnification produced by a plane mirror is
questions.explanation: A plane mirror produces an image of the same size as the object. Therefore, the linear magnification is 1.

questions.question: A boy stands 3m in front of a plane mirror. What is the distance between the boy and his image?
questions.explanation: The image is 3 m behind the mirror. The distance between the boy (3 m in front) and his image (3 m behind) is 3 + 3 = 6 m.

questions.question: The characteristic of a plane mirror image in which left appears as right is called
questions.explanation: In a plane mirror, the left side of the object appears as the right side of the image. This phenomenon is called lateral inversion.

questions.question: Two plane mirrors are inclined at 60° to each other. Calculate the number of images formed.
questions.explanation: For two mirrors inclined at angle θ, the number of images is given by n = 360/θ − 1. Here θ = 60°, so n = 360/60 − 1 = 6 − 1 = 5.

questions.question: Two plane mirrors are inclined at 90° to each other. The number of images formed is
If two plane mirrors are placed parallel and facing each other, the number of images formed is
questions.explanation: When two plane mirrors are parallel and facing each other, multiple reflections occur, producing an infinite number of images.

questions.question: When a plane mirror is rotated through an angle θ, the reflected ray is rotated through
questions.explanation: When a plane mirror is rotated through an angle θ, the reflected ray rotates through 2θ. This is a standard result of reflection geometry.

questions.question: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror at a glancing angle of 40°. Calculate the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray.
questions.explanation: The angle of incidence is 40°. The angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is given by 180° − 2i = 180° − 80° = 100°.

questions.question: A concave mirror is also known as a
questions.explanation: A concave mirror converges parallel rays of light to a focus. Therefore, it is also called a converging mirror.

questions.question: A convex mirror is also known as a
questions.explanation: A convex mirror diverges parallel rays of light as if they came from a focus behind the mirror. Therefore, it is called a diverging mirror.

questions.question: The focal length of a spherical mirror is
options: Equal to the radius of curvature
One-quarter of the radius of curvature
questions.explanation: For a spherical mirror, the focal length f is related to the radius of curvature R by f = R/2. So f is half the radius of curvature.

questions.question: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 20cm. Calculate its focal length.
questions.explanation: Using f = R/2, with R = 20 cm, f = 20/2 = 10 cm.

questions.question: The mirror formula is given by
questions.explanation: The mirror formula is 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, where f is focal length, u is object distance, and v is image distance.

questions.question: The linear magnification of a mirror is given by
questions.explanation: The linear magnification produced by a mirror is m = v/u, where v is image distance and u is object distance.

questions.question: An object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. The image formed is
questions.explanation: When the object is at the centre of curvature C of a concave mirror, the image is formed at C. It is real, inverted, and of the same size as the object.

questions.question: An object is placed at the principal focus of a concave mirror. The image formed is at
questions.explanation: When an object is placed at the principal focus F of a concave mirror, the reflected rays are parallel, so the image is formed at infinity.

questions.question: An object is placed between the principal focus and the pole of a concave mirror. The image formed is
questions.explanation: When the object is between F and the pole of a concave mirror, the image is virtual, erect, and magnified. This is the principle of a shaving mirror.

questions.question: An object is placed beyond the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. The image formed is
questions.explanation: When the object is beyond C of a concave mirror, the image is formed between F and C. It is real, inverted, and diminished.

questions.question: An object is placed between the centre of curvature and the principal focus of a concave mirror. The image formed is
questions.explanation: When the object is between C and F of a concave mirror, the image is formed beyond C. It is real, inverted, and magnified.

questions.question: The image formed by a convex mirror is always
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image, regardless of the object position.

questions.question: A concave mirror is used as a shaving mirror because it produces
options: A magnified, erect virtual image when the face is close
questions.explanation: When the face is placed between the focus and the pole of a concave mirror, it produces a magnified, erect virtual image, making it ideal for shaving.

questions.question: A convex mirror is used as a driving mirror because it
options: Gives a wide field of view
questions.explanation: A convex mirror gives a wide field of view and always forms an erect, diminished virtual image, making it useful as a driving mirror.

questions.question: A concave mirror is used in a searchlight to produce
questions.explanation: When a source is placed at the principal focus of a concave mirror, the reflected rays emerge as a parallel beam of light, which is useful in searchlights.

questions.question: The image formed on a screen is always
questions.explanation: A real image can be formed on a screen because the light rays actually converge at the image point. Virtual images cannot be formed on a screen.

questions.question: An object is placed 20cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10cm. Calculate the image distance.
An object is placed 15cm from a concave mirror of focal length 10cm. Calculate the image distance.
An object is placed 10cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 10cm. The image distance is
questions.explanation:
For a convex mirror, f is negative. f = −10 cm, u = 10 cm.
1/f = 1/u + 1/v ⇒ 1/(−10) = 1/10 + 1/v
1/v = −1/10 − 1/10 = −2/10 = −1/5
v = −5 cm (image is 5 cm behind the mirror).

questions.question: The image of an object placed 5cm from a concave mirror of focal length 10cm is formed at
questions.explanation:
Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, with f = 10 cm and u = 5 cm:
1/10 = 1/5 + 1/v
1/v = 1/10 − 1/5 = −1/10
v = −10 cm, so the image is 10 cm behind the mirror (virtual).

questions.question: A concave mirror of focal length 15cm forms a real image three times the size of the object. Calculate the object distance.
questions.explanation:
For a real image, magnification m = −3 (inverted). Using m = −v/u, we get v = 3u.
Mirror formula: 1/15 = 1/u + 1/(3u) = 4/(3u)
3u = 60 ⇒ u = 20 cm.

questions.question: The linear magnification produced by a concave mirror that forms a real image twice the size of the object is
questions.explanation: Magnification is the ratio of image size to object size. A real image twice the size has a magnification magnitude of 2 (negative sign indicates inversion).

questions.question: The radius of curvature of a concave mirror is 30cm. What is its focal length?
questions.explanation: Using f = R/2, with R = 30 cm, f = 30/2 = 15 cm.

questions.question: A concave mirror can form a virtual image when the object is placed
options: Between the principal focus and the pole
questions.explanation: A concave mirror forms a virtual, erect, magnified image when the object is placed between the principal focus and the pole.

questions.question: A ray of light passing through the centre of curvature of a concave mirror is reflected
questions.explanation: A ray passing through the centre of curvature C is incident normally on the mirror, so it reflects back along the same path.

questions.question: A ray of light parallel to the principal axis of a concave mirror after reflection passes through the
questions.explanation: By definition, a ray parallel to the principal axis of a concave mirror reflects and passes through the principal focus F.

questions.question: A ray of light passing through the principal focus of a concave mirror after reflection
options: Passes through the centre of curvature
Becomes parallel to the principal axis
questions.explanation: A ray passing through the principal focus F of a concave mirror reflects and becomes parallel to the principal axis.

questions.question: The focal length of a convex mirror is taken as
questions.explanation: By sign convention, the focal length of a convex mirror is negative because its focus is behind the mirror.

questions.question: In the mirror formula, the image distance v is positive for
questions.explanation: By sign convention, real images are formed in front of the mirror, so v is positive. Virtual images have negative v.

questions.question: An object 4cm high is placed 15cm from a concave mirror of focal length 5cm. Calculate the size of the image.
questions.explanation:
Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v: 1/5 = 1/15 + 1/v ⇒ 1/v = 1/5 − 1/15 = 2/15 ⇒ v = 7.5 cm.
Magnification m = −v/u = −7.5/15 = −0.5.
Image size = |m| × object size = 0.5 × 4 = 2 cm.

questions.question: A converging mirror has a focal length of 20cm. If an object is placed 40cm from it, the image is
questions.explanation:
Using 1/20 = 1/40 + 1/v ⇒ 1/v = 1/20 − 1/40 = 1/40 ⇒ v = 40 cm.
Magnification m = −v/u = −40/40 = −1. The image is real, inverted, and of the same size.

questions.question: A convex mirror of focal length 12cm produces an image 6cm behind the mirror. Calculate the object distance.
questions.explanation:
For a convex mirror, f = −12 cm and image distance v = −6 cm (behind mirror).
1/f = 1/u + 1/v ⇒ −1/12 = 1/u − 1/6
1/u = −1/12 + 1/6 = 1/12 ⇒ u = 12 cm.

questions.question: The image of an object formed by a convex mirror is always located
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual image behind the mirror.

questions.question: Which type of mirror is used as a dentist's mirror?
questions.explanation: A dentist uses a concave mirror to obtain a magnified, erect virtual image of the teeth.

questions.question: A plane mirror is moved 1m towards a man standing 4m in front of it. The distance between the man and his new image is
questions.explanation: Initially, the man is 4 m from the mirror. After moving the mirror 1 m towards him, the distance becomes 3 m. The image is 3 m behind the mirror, so the distance between the man and his image is 3 + 3 = 6 m.
